_**Agent (claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking)**_

Here's my analysis and proposed algorithm. The core problem is clear from the code: `fret_detect.c` uses a flat hysteresis comparator — press below 2500, release above 2800. Rapid re-presses that only rise to ~2600-2700 between strikes never cross the release threshold, so the second note is invisible. Lowering the press threshold to compensate lets the idle ripple trigger false presses.

The fix is to detect **relative movement** (rise-then-fall) within the pressed state, rather than requiring the signal to return to an absolute release threshold. Combined with EMA smoothing to tame the ripple, this separates genuine re-presses from noise.

  "plan": "# Slope-Aware Fret Detection Algorithm\n\n## Problem\n\nThe current detector in [fret_detect.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_detect.c) is a simple hysteresis comparator:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;c\nif (val \u003c press_threshold)   → pressed\nif (val \u003e release_threshold) → released\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis creates two conflicting failure modes:\n- **Rapid repeated notes**: Signal rises partway between presses (e.g., to 2650) but never reaches the release threshold (2800), so the second press is invisible.\n- **Idle ripple false triggers**: Lowering thresholds to catch shallow re-presses lets the continuous ripple on the unpressed signal generate spurious press events.\n\n## Approach: EMA + Relative-Movement State Machine\n\nTwo complementary techniques:\n\n1. **EMA smoothing** reduces the effective ripple amplitude, widening the gap between noise and real signal movement.\n2. **Relative thresholds** (rise-from-trough, fall-from-peak) detect re-presses without requiring the signal to return to an absolute level.\n\n### State Machine\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nstateDiagram-v2\n    IDLE --\u003e PRESSED: smoothed \u003c press threshold\n    PRESSED --\u003e IDLE: smoothed \u003e release threshold\n    PRESSED --\u003e RISING: smoothed \u003e trough + repress_delta\n    RISING --\u003e IDLE: smoothed \u003e release threshold\n    RISING --\u003e PRESSED: smoothed \u003c peak - repress_fall\\n(RE-PRESS: emit new press event)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Per-channel state:**\n\n| Field | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| &#96;smoothed&#96; | EMA-filtered ADC value |\n| &#96;prev_smoothed&#96; | Previous smoothed (for slope / debugging) |\n| &#96;trough&#96; | Min smoothed value since entering PRESSED |\n| &#96;peak&#96; | Max smoothed value since entering RISING |\n| &#96;pressed&#96; | Currently in pressed state |\n| &#96;rising&#96; | Signal has risen repress_delta above trough |\n\n### Detection Logic (per channel, per update)\n\n1. **EMA update**: &#96;smoothed += (raw - smoothed) \u003e\u003e 2&#96; (alpha = 0.25, ~8ms group delay at 500 Hz)\n\n2. **IDLE state**: If &#96;smoothed \u003c press&#96; threshold, transition to PRESSED. Record trough = smoothed. Emit press event.\n\n3. **PRESSED state** (not rising):\n   - Track &#96;trough = min(trough, smoothed)&#96;\n   - If &#96;smoothed \u003e release&#96; threshold → full RELEASE back to IDLE\n   - If &#96;smoothed \u003e trough + repress_delta&#96; → enter RISING, set &#96;peak = smoothed&#96;\n\n4. **RISING state** (re-press armed):\n   - Track &#96;peak = max(peak, smoothed)&#96;\n   - If &#96;smoothed \u003e release&#96; threshold → full RELEASE to IDLE\n   - If &#96;smoothed \u003c peak - repress_fall&#96; → **re-press detected**: emit new press event, reset &#96;trough = smoothed&#96;, return to PRESSED\n\n### Why This Handles Both Failure Modes\n\n**Rapid notes**: After a press, the signal rises partially (say, by 300 counts from the trough). Once it exceeds &#96;repress_delta&#96; (250), the RISING state arms. When the signal peaks and falls back by &#96;repress_fall&#96; (150), a new press event fires — even though the signal never reached the absolute release threshold.\n\n**Idle ripple**: The EMA with alpha=0.25 attenuates high-frequency ripple by 50-70%, reducing +-100 raw ripple to roughly +-40 smoothed. Since &#96;repress_delta&#96; (250) is far above the smoothed ripple amplitude, the RISING state is never entered during a sustained press. And the absolute press threshold still gates initial detection.\n\n### New Threshold Struct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;c\ntypedef struct {\n    uint16_t press;\n    uint16_t release;\n    uint16_t repress_delta;  // min rise from trough to arm re-press\n    uint16_t repress_fall;   // min fall from peak to confirm re-press\n} fret_threshold_t;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Default Values (starting point, will need tuning)\n\n| Fret | press | release | repress_delta | repress_fall |\n|------|-------|---------|---------------|--------------|\n| Green | 2500 | 2800 | 250 | 150 |\n| Red | 2500 | 2800 | 250 | 150 |\n| Yellow | 1500 | 1700 | 180 | 120 |\n| Blue | 1500 | 1700 | 180 | 120 |\n| Orange | 2000 | 2200 | 200 | 130 |\n\n### Re-press Event Semantics\n\nA re-press emits **only a new press flag** (no release flag). This is correct for Guitar Hero: holding a fret and strumming repeatedly counts as separate notes. The [fret_button.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c) chord accumulation already handles this — each press event opens a new chord window and queues a new strum. The fret output pin stays asserted throughout, which is the desired behavior.\n\nWhen the fret is eventually fully released (smoothed \u003e release threshold), a normal release event fires and [fret_button.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c) handles the delayed pin release as before.\n\n### Additional: Smoothed Value Getter\n\nAdd &#96;fret_detect_smoothed(fret_channel_t ch)&#96; to expose the EMA-filtered value for the data stream / tuner tool, enabling visual verification of smoothing effectiveness.\n\n## Files to Change\n\n- [firmware/fretboard/fret_detect.h](firmware/fretboard/fret_detect.h) — Expand &#96;fret_threshold_t&#96; with &#96;repress_delta&#96;/&#96;repress_fall&#96;, add &#96;fret_detect_smoothed()&#96; prototype\n- [firmware/fretboard/fret_detect.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_detect.c) — Replace threshold comparator with EMA + state machine\n\nNo changes needed to [fret_button.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c), [fret_scan.c](firmware/fretboard/fret_scan.c), or [main.c](firmware/fretboard/main.c).\n\n## Tuning Notes\n\nThe &#96;repress_delta&#96; and &#96;repress_fall&#96; values are educated guesses.   "plan": "# Slope-Aware Fret Detection (PC-Side)\n\n## Problem\n\nThe current detectors fail on two conflicting scenarios:\n- **Rapid repeated notes**: Signal doesn't return to the absolute release threshold between presses, so the second note is never detected\n- **Sustained notes with ripple**: Lowering thresholds to catch shallow re-presses lets idle ripple cause false triggers\n\n## Solution: EMA + Relative-Movement State Machine\n\n### New file: [detect_slope.py](tools/fret-tuner/detect_slope.py)\n\nA new pluggable detector following the existing contract in [SPEC.md](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md). All three changes are in place and lint-clean. Here's a summary of what was done:

**New file: `tools/fret-tuner/detect_slope.py`**

The new pluggable detector implements:

- **EMA smoothing** in integer fixed-point (8 fractional bits, no floats). The raw ADC is filtered with a configurable alpha (default 25%, tunable from the UI). This attenuates idle ripple by ~50-70% while keeping latency around 2-3 samples (4-6ms).

- **Three-state FSM** per channel:
  - **IDLE** -- waiting for `smoothed < press` threshold
  - **PRESSED** -- tracks `trough` (running minimum). If signal rises by `repress_delta` above the trough, transitions to RISING
  - **RISING** -- tracks `peak` (running maximum). If signal falls by `repress_fall` from the peak, that inflection confirms a **re-press** without requiring a full return to the release threshold. If signal reaches the release threshold, it's a full release back to IDLE.

- **`press_count`** in output -- increments on every initial press and re-press, giving the actuator a reliable edge signal.

**Modified: `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py`**

The edge detection loop now checks for `press_count` changes to detect re-presses. When a detector doesn't provide `press_count` (like the existing `detect_threshold` and `detect_trough`), it falls back to the original `pressed` bool comparison. Fully backward compatible.

Yes, that's coming from the detection logic. The shading is driven by the `pressed` field in the detector output, and during a re-press sequence `pressed` never goes `False` — the state machine goes PRESSED → RISING → PRESSED, never back through IDLE. So the UI sees one continuous `pressed = True` and draws a single unbroken shaded region, even though `press_count` is correctly incrementing for each individual note.

The detection itself is working (the actuator sees each `press_count` change and fires separate strums). It's purely a visualization gap — the chart has no way to show note boundaries within a continuous press region right now.

If you want to see each note as a separate shaded block, there are two options:

1. **UI-side** (cleaner): Update `index.html` to use `press_count` changes to draw vertical markers or break the shading at re-press boundaries
2. **Detector-side** (quick hack): Emit `pressed = False` for the single sample at the re-press inflection point, so the shading naturally gaps — but this briefly reports "not pressed" which could confuse the actuator's release scheduling

Want me to do either of these, or is the current visualization good enough since the actual note detection is working?

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>

Here's what the cooldown does:

**The problem**: With low `repress_delta` and `repress_fall`, every ripple cycle during the initial rise of a sustain triggers a false re-press. Each cycle is only ~4-10ms, well within the sustain holdoff, so they all pass the holdoff check.

**The fix**: `REPRESS_COOLDOWN_MS` (default 40ms) blocks the PRESSED→RISING transition until enough time has elapsed since the last press event. This prevents the rapid-fire false triggers during the rise phase. The signal must settle in PRESSED for at least the cooldown period before re-press detection arms.

- **Rapid notes** still work: real notes are typically 50-200ms apart, well above the 40ms cooldown
- **Sustain rise**: ripple-induced false triggers are suppressed because each would try to re-arm within <10ms
- **Sustain dip**: still handled by the existing holdoff (the signal plateaus for 300ms, far exceeding the holdoff)

The new slider `REPRESS_COOLDOWN_MS` will appear in the UI. Just switch away from `detect_slope` and back to hot-reload the detector.
